summary: Adaptive prefetch threshold caused latency spikes with per-route quant profile mismatch; need safe traffic-exit and rollback guidance
description:
Issue summary:
HelixHealth observed an abrupt 95th and 99th percentile latency increase following our runtime's adaptive prefetch threshold update combined with a per-route 8-bit quant profile. The customer is on Dedicated capacity in us-east and reported degraded production SLAs for critical inference routes (medical-summarization and triage-chat).

Impact:
- 95p latency increased from ~420ms to ~2.4s on two routes.
- 99p tail rose to ~4.1s.
- Small but steady 5xx spike from baseline 0.02% to 1.8% within a 30m window.
- Customer-facing errors and timeouts causing partial outage for automated triage flows.

Why this ticket: The customer suspects the adaptive prefetch threshold mechanic increased aggressive KV cache eviction when mixed with a new per-route quant profile, producing repeated cold-prefetches and amplification of tail latency. They need a safe, low-risk exit plan to return to stable latency while preserving tenant isolation and without a full model revert.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer runs sustained mixed-length chat workload against route 'triage-chat' pinned to openllm-redwood-quant-8bit.
2) System warmup occurs then traffic pattern shifts to lots of short prompts followed by occasional long summaries.
3) After adaptive prefetch threshold update (flag enabled), observed periodic bursts of long latencies and 5xx.
4) Reproduce window captured between 2026-03-12T09:20-09:55 UTC in customer logs.
logs:
[2026-03-12T09:23:12Z] request_id=abc123 route=triage-chat model=openllm-redwood-quant-8bit result=timeout latency=4100ms
[2026-03-12T09:23:13Z] serving-runtime WARN kv-cache: evicted session_id=xyz due_to=prefetch_threshold
[2026-03-12T09:24:05Z] request_id=def456 route=medical-summarization model=gpt-neox-20b result=200 latency=2400ms
[2026-03-12T09:24:05Z] scheduler INFO batch_size=1 reason=cache-miss
[2026-03-12T09:25:00Z] prometheus metric:serve_5xx_rate{route="triage-chat"} 0.018
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Adaptive prefetch threshold lowered the retention window for small sessions causing frequent cold KV cache misses for mixed-length sessions.

Hypothesis 2: Per-route quant profile 'openllm-redwood-quant-8bit' has slightly different memory footprint, causing eviction heuristics to trigger earlier per-GPU leading to scheduling fallback to single-request batches.
Telemetry: tenant's per-GPU memory pressure spiked coincident with eviction logs. GPU memory pressure reported ~78% to ~96% in the 09:20-09:30 window.

Reproduction attempts on staging with identical load reproduced tail latency only when both adaptive prefetch flag and per-route quant profile were active. Disabling either flag removed spike in staging.
Risk assessment: Full model revert for dedicated tenant requires capacity coordination and ~45m of redistribution; customer wants lower-risk immediate mitigation.

Suggested immediate mitigations: 1) Temporarily increase prefetch retention threshold for this tenant to previous value. 2) Force route to use fallback quant profile (higher precision) for a rolling minute to observe impact. 3) If safe, move heavy long-form requests to a separate scaled pool (traffic-shed) while restoring baseline settings.
comments: 2026-03-12 10:05 - Ethan Cole (Support): Customer submitted heap and perf traces. They cannot tolerate >1s 95p latency on triage-chat; asking for a hotpath rollback option.
2026-03-12 10:22 - Maya Patel (SRE): I'm seeing eviction stamps in the runtime logs matching customer timestamps. Preparing an emergency config toggle that targets only this tenant route.

2026-03-12 11:03 - Eng on-call (R. Alvarez): Confirmed quant profile causes ~12% increase in token decode memory for 8-bit path under our kernel selection. Proposing traffic-split 90/10 to fallback model as an experiment before global revert.

2026-03-12 11:47 - Ethan Cole (Support): Customer agreed to a staged traffic-split and prefers we avoid full capacity redistribution during business hours. Approved 90/10 traffic-split to fallback model for 20 minutes as test.

2026-03-13 08:15 - Maya Patel (SRE): Executed tenant-scoped prefetch retention increase (rollback to baseline) at 2026-03-13T08:12 UTC. Initial telemetry shows 95p decreased to ~480ms within 6 minutes. Monitoring continues.
resolution: Triage in progress. Temporary tenant-scoped prefetch retention increase applied as low-risk mitigation; follow-up steps include a controlled 90/10 traffic split to fallback quant profile and coordinated capacity rehydration if needed. Final resolution pending post-observability window and customer sign-off.
